requirements: Classify every unused blade and both solder tails as real primary metal, even though it has no net ID. Unused secondary pins remain isolated-region conductors.
Enforce across both copper layers, vias, pads, fills and exposed/assembled solder; do not rely solely on same-layer net-class DRC.
Include primary-to-hardware/controller/cable conductors and shortest paths around edges/holes. No soldermask or coating insulation credit.
U1 crosses the boundary only through its qualified input/output construction; K1 only through qualified coil/contact construction. Never route across the barrier beneath them.
Any needed isolation slot changes source-owned outline/hole geometry and requires a source revision/ECO, not an undeclared native cut.

requirements: Use distinct primary/isolated net classes; the separate 8/3.2 mm rules override ordinary low-voltage fabrication clearances.
Current/width/via/thermal allocations are specified by the mains thermal/stencil design before routing. No controller USB or buck nets/classes are imported.
Keep RV1 loop at J1 and RC beside J4; filter LINE and LOAD pairs remain at opposite edges and do not share a surge return through the isolated region.
Route U2 programming returns separately from IN/OUT and clamp-current loops; join near GND pin8.
The 0.15 mm ordinary isolated clearance stays below the 0.1995 mm computed lower bound for U2 escapes; the 8/3.2 mm isolation and primary rules always override it.

Use 2 mm primary routes and widen J1-RV1 surge paths to at least 3 mm where pad transitions allow. Join both Sabre tails per blade with solid copper. These are initial routing allocations; fuse-clearing integral, inrush duration and MOV pulse survival require separate routed-copper verification.
params.verification: Saved class assignments and actual route, current, return and thermal review.
params.status: Declared routing allocations; independent final review, native application and current/fault acceptance pending.
